clue.text: Event formerly requiring work on winter sport vessel by record-holder in a bad mood

indicators.note: the string of work, sport, vessel and record-holder sits inside the word for a bad mood

parts.note: to have the hump is to be sulky
OP is short for opus, a work
skiing is a winter sport
a pan is a cooking vessel
a disc jockey holds the records he plays

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned contest once demanded labour on a ski boat from a sulking champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' looks like an athletics champion, fitting the event, but it is a disc jockey. The triple jump used to be called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The athletics discipline now called the triple jump was earlier known by this three-phase descriptive name.

clue.text: Success with article takes nerve, so get liquored up

parts.note: a hit is a success
the definite article
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: Writing a successful article takes courage, so the writer goes off for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start drinking heavily, which is exactly what becoming drunk involves.

clue.text: African knife for 11, swallowing his tail?

indicators.note: the word swallows its own final letter, which is taken off the end and put inside

parts.note: 11-across is HEATHEN, and a heathen is a pagan

explanation.surface: Someone asks which African blade suits a heathen who is eating his own tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter N moves from the end of PAGAN to its middle, giving PA-N-GA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panga is a broad heavy machete used in East Africa for cutting brush.

clue.text: Types holding unusual sash enter office

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged
one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: types are kinds
the letters of sash, shuffled

explanation.surface: Printing types contain an odd sash as someone takes up a post.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a new minister formally kisses the monarch's hands on taking office.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing hands is the ceremony by which a British Prime Minister or minister formally takes up their appointment.

clue.text: Flags of convenience in the wet garden

definitions.text: Flags of convenience in the wet garden

parts.note: surface reading: flags flown by ships registered abroad for cheapness
setter's reading: flat stones you step on to keep your feet dry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags of convenience' suggests shipping registration, but flags are also flat slabs; in a sodden garden they are convenient to walk on.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are flat slabs laid as a path, handy footing across muddy lawn.

clue.text: Horse in wet weather returning to Indian islands

indicators.note: the horse goes inside the weather word
in a down clue, returning means the weather word is read back upwards

parts.note: rain is wet weather
a cob is a sturdy horse

explanation.surface: A horse out in the rain heads back to islands in India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicobar Islands are an Indian archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, grouped with the Andamans.

clue.text: Scots island, left and naturally right

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'relating to rights'

parts.note: Jura is an island in the Inner Hebrides
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Scottish island lies on the left, and of course on the right too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left and right' look like a pair of directions; right is the definition, in the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Jural describes matters of law, especially legal rights and obligations.

clue.text: A jewel turns up — sounds like there's another — a lot of work needed

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the words bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a jewel

indicators.note: the second jewel is one that only sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: another jewel, but spoken rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A gem surfaces and another seems to follow, but much effort is required.
explanation.walkthrough: The joule is the unit of work or energy in physics, pronounced like jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A megajoule is a million joules, a large quantity of energy or work in physics.

clue.text: See 4
Evil grips a cleaner at scene of tea party?

indicators.note: one word grips the other by holding it inside

parts.note: vice is wickedness
taken as written
a rag is used for cleaning

explanation.surface: Something wicked seizes a charwoman at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: The vicarage tea party is a cosy English stereotype, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson's house is the traditional setting for a genteel parish tea gathering in English life.

clue.text: Opportunity like 27: live it up with Walesa in ecstasy

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for ecstasy

parts.note: a trance is a state of ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for live is read upwards

parts.note: to be is to live; 'it' is read with the verb
Lech Walesa, the Polish Solidarity leader

explanation.surface: A chance to celebrate with Lech Walesa in rapture, like the alliance clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is TRIPLE ALLIANCE, and treble means triple. The treble chance was the main bet on the British football pools.
explanation.definitionFit: The treble chance was a football pools bet offering a big win, so a three-fold opportunity.

clue.text: Rechauffé chicken, not at the foregoing?

parts.note: réchauffé means reheated; to heat is to warm up
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Warmed-up chicken, which nobody serves at the event just mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The foregoing' is the previous clue, 9-across VICARAGE: an unbeliever would not be found at the vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever stays away from church affairs, so would not be at the parson's home.

clue.text: Phone call to jolt a protector in the lab

parts.note: to give someone a bell is to phone them
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A telephone call gives a shock to someone guarding a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give me a bell' is British slang for 'phone me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a glass dome placed over apparatus or specimens in laboratories to shield them.

clue.text: Meaty writer in modern art

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Francis ... the essayist, whose name is a meat
second meaning: Francis ... the twentieth-century painter

explanation.surface: A writer with real substance features in contemporary art.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous Francis Bacons: the Elizabethan essayist and philosopher, and the Irish-born painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to an Elizabethan essayist and to a celebrated twentieth-century painter, and also names cured pork.

clue.text: Pitman displaying singular charity when taken in by forger

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it

parts.note: a coiner makes counterfeit money
alms is charity; made singular it loses its S

explanation.surface: A miner shows rare generosity when a counterfeiter cons him.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitman is a worker in a pit, a colliery, so someone digging coal underground.

clue.text: "I'm proud to be mother" subedited

indicators.note: editing rearranges text, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the first three letters of the word are fodder; the rest is the signal

explanation.surface: A quoted proud boast about motherhood that a sub-editor has tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subedited' looks like one word but splits into fodder and signal. Proud here means sticking out, as in 'stick out like a sore thumb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conspicuous sticks out like an injured digit, and proud means protruding.

clue.text: Top people like 27 having some success fighting some of the Irish

indicators.note: only some of the success word is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: a triumph is a success

indicators.note: only part of the nationality word is kept, its end cut off

parts.note: V for versus, as in a fight between two sides
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leaders like an alliance enjoy partial victory battling a few of the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is TRIPLE ALLIANCE: triumviri were ruling groups of three in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rome a triumvirate was three magistrates or rulers sharing power, so a trio of leaders.

clue.text: Change Poles for getting into the car

indicators.note: the pieces get into the vehicle, so they sit inside its word

parts.note: a tramcar, often just called a car
north and south are the poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people swap places so they can climb into the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it is the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter something completely, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Mole wandering around a government department long ago?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'of long ago'

indicators.note: the letters wander out of their order
the jumbled letters go around the department

parts.note: the letters of mole, shuffled
the Department of Trade and Industry, a former UK ministry

explanation.surface: A spy roams about a Whitehall ministry, in some bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is a spy planted in an organisation, which fits a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time describes things belonging to a bygone era, so something from former days.

clue.text: Film producer gets fuel from yarrow

indicators.note: a producer makes something new out of the material, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: the letters of film, rearranged
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A movie maker extracts fuel from a wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Milfoil is another name for yarrow, the feathery-leaved plant Achillea millefolium.

clue.text: Name for a dove, perhaps, in dire need

indicators.note: the name sits inside the next words, running across them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Choosing a name for a pet dove when desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: Irene comes from the Greek for peace, and the dove symbolises peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name means peace in Greek, so it suits the bird that stands for peace.

clue.text: Small creature in cover, not the whole hog?

indicators.note: the creature sits inside the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a mite is a tiny creature

explanation.surface: A tiny animal hides under a lid, and it's only part of a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going the whole hog' means doing something completely; restricted is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted stops short of going all the way, the opposite of going the whole hog.

clue.text: Miserable specimen takes article from port

indicators.note: takes from means removes from, so the article comes away

parts.note: Antwerp is a major Belgian port
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wretched individual steals an item from a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or contemptible person, a feeble example of humanity.

clue.text: Meaty writer spoiled the walk

indicators.note: something spoiled is messed up, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: Charles Lamb, the essayist, whose name is a meat
the letters of the, rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer of substance ruined the stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lambeth Walk is a 1930s London Cockney song and dance. Compare 13-across, the other meaty writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth, a London district, gives its name to a famous Cockney strutting dance called a walk.

clue.text: Sprightly renderings of the conclusion

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
fin is Spanish and French for end

explanation.surface: Lively versions of an ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renderings' means translations: Spanish 'el fin' is 'the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small, delicate and lively like an elf, so impish and sprightly.

clue.text: Artistic friar speaks of girl to the victor of Jutland

indicators.note: speaking the names out loud gives the sound needed

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Admiral Jellicoe commanded the British fleet at the Battle of Jutland, 1916

explanation.surface: A painting monk talks of a young woman to the admiral who won at Jutland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Jellicoe was also a real playwright, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Fra Angelico was a Dominican friar and early Renaissance Florentine painter.

clue.text: Home games? You cannot be serious

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase, 'not seriously'

parts.note: being in is being at home
fun and games

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of home matches, as if joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You cannot be serious' is John McEnroe's famous protest at Wimbledon, so the games look like tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something jokingly means it is not meant seriously, matching the disbelieving protest.

clue.text: League like 1 across, come to grief with loyal one breaking weapon

indicators.note: the number breaks into the weapon, splitting it to sit inside

parts.note: to trip is to stumble and fall
leal is a Scots word for loyal
a lance is a weapon
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pact like the jump event collapses when a faithful ally shatters a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 1-across is the old name of the triple jump, so 'like 1 across' means triple. The Triple Alliance joined Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy before 1914.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance, and this one had three members, like the three-part jump.
